'''Michael Earl Conrad''' (1941–2000) was an American theoretical biologist.<ref>[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?arnumber=910460 Obituary in ''IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation'' 5(1), 2001.]</ref> He was a professor of computer science at [[Wayne State University]].<ref>[http://alumni.stanford.edu/get/page/magazine/article/?article_id=39403 Obituary in ''Stanford Magazine'']</ref> His book ''Adaptability'' (1983) has been very influential in [[theoretical biology]].<ref>[[Robert Rosen (theoretical biologist)|Robert Rosen]] 1986. [Review.] ''Bulletin of Mathematical Biology'' 48(5/6): 701–703.</ref>  

Conrad was the first to publish theory on the evolution of [[evolvability]], beginning in 1972,<ref name="Conrad:1972:Importance">{{cite journal |  title=The importance of molecular hierarchy in information processing |   author=Conrad, Michael |  editor=C.H. Waddington | journal=Towards a Theoretical Biology |   volume=4 |   pages=222 |   year=1972 |   publisher=Edinburgh University Press Edinburgh}}</ref> with the idea that mutations which smoothed the [[adaptive landscape]] would increase the chance that other adaptive mutations could be continually produced, and would thereby hitchhike along with those mutations, thus "bootstrapping the adaptive landscape"<ref>{{cite journal | author = Conrad, Michael | year = 1979 | title = Bootstrapping on the adaptive landscape | journal = BioSystems | volume = 11 | issue = 2–3 | pages = 167–182 | doi=10.1016/0303-2647(79)90009-1| pmid = 497367 | hdl = 2027.42/23514 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> to produce the "self-facilitation of evolution".<ref name=Conrad:and:Volkenstein:1981>{{cite journal | author = Conrad, Michael and Volkenstein, MV | year = 1981 | title = Replaceability of amino acids and the self-facilitation of evolution | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 92 |   number=3 | pages = 293–299 |   publisher=Elsevier | doi=10.1016/0022-5193(81)90293-9| pmid = 7329083 | bibcode = 1981JThBi..92..293C }}</ref>

== Career ==

Conrad received his A.B. in Biology at [[Harvard University]] in 1964.  He entered [[Stanford University Medical School]] but was persuaded by faculty there to pursue a Ph.D. in Biophysics with Professor [[Howard H. Pattee]], which he obtained in 1969.  

Conrad continued with postdoctoral research at the Center for Theoretical Studies at the University of Miami, and the Department of Mathematics at the University of California at Berkeley working with [[Hans-Joachim Bremermann|Hans Bremermann]].  Not finding theoretical biology positions in the United States, Conrad took an Assistant Professorship at the new Institute for Information Processing at the [[University of Tubingen]] in 1973, and a temporary position with the Logic of Computers group in the Department of Computer Science and Communication at the [[University of Michigan at Ann Arbor]].  

Conrad finally obtained a tenure-track position in the Computer Science department of [[Wayne State University]] in 1979, where he remained for the rest of his career.<ref name="Pattee2002">{{cite journal |last1=Pattee |first1=Howard |title=The origins of Michael Conrad's research programs (1964–1979) |journal=BioSystems |date=2002 |volume=64 |issue=1–3 |pages=5–11|doi=10.1016/S0303-2647(01)00169-1 |pmid=11755483 }}</ref>
